text:
Travis Sanheim plays almost 25 minutes a night for Philadelphia and does a bit of everything with them: 10 points in 27 games, 54 blocked shots, and three goals in his last ten, including the third-period go-ahead goal against Buffalo on November 17. The assists have dried up in that stretch, though, with none in ten games.

His numbers are honest. He has four goals on 4.09 expected goals, our measure of chance quality, so there's no finishing luck to give back, and the Flyers have been 4.48 points better in five-on-five expected goals share with him on the ice than without him. NHL EDGE puts his top shot at 95.7 mph, 92nd percentile, and his skating distance in the 98th. Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd of 215 defensemen last season at 2.3 wins above replacement, facing top competition, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows him jumping into the rush on 33% of his shots, almost double the typical defenseman. Our numbers project 33 points. The last game was rough: a 7-3 loss in Washington.
headline: Sanheim, the Flyers' minute-eater
